issues.description: import-notation 'url' branch returns early when params contain url(), silently skipping the case it should validate.
issues.detail: The guard `if (primary === 'url' && /url\(/i.test(params)) return;` inverts logic: under primary='url' the walker should still examine params containing url() for malformed or non-standard content. The branch should mirror the 'string' branch and skip only when there is nothing to check. This is a correctness regression, not just a missed fast path.

issues.description: HAS_PERCENTAGE and HAS_KEYWORD use asymmetric case-sensitivity flags with no stated invariant.
issues.detail: In keyframe-selector-notation, HAS_KEYWORD uses /i but HAS_PERCENTAGE does not. The prefilter must be a strict superset of cases the walker would flag; the asymmetry is unjustified and undocumented. Either normalize the flags or state the invariant explaining why the difference is safe.

issues.description: font-weight-notation HAS_NAMED/HAS_NUMERIC guards misread mixed-value font shorthand.
issues.detail: When primary is 'numeric', the guard returns early if no named keyword is present, but a 'font' shorthand value can contain both a named weight and a numeric one. The predicate conflates 'value contains a named keyword' with 'value is named', risking false negatives. The invariant 'every value the parser would flag also matches the prefilter' must be stated and verified.

issues.description: Regexes built from keyword Sets/Maps lack literal-escaping, fragile to future additions.
issues.detail: HAS_NAMED, HAS_NUMERIC, HAS_PERCENTAGE, and HAS_KEYWORD interpolate set/map contents directly into RegExp source. Today's alphanumeric/percent contents are safe, but a future keyword containing a regex metacharacter would silently corrupt the pattern. Add an escapeRegExp helper or annotate the precondition 'all keywords are [a-z]+'.

issues.description: media-feature-range-notation prefilter /(?:min|max)-/i is an over-approximation presented as a specification.
issues.detail: The pattern matches anywhere in atRule.params, including custom identifiers, calc expressions, or vendor tokens. As a pre-filter this is correctness-safe (false positives only cost work), but the comment should explicitly mark it as a heuristic so future readers do not tighten it incorrectly.

issues.description: No new regression tests pin the early-exit boundaries and no performance numbers justify the change.
issues.detail: The diff adds fast-path returns across six rules with no targeted tests asserting (a) early-exit fires when expected and (b) boundary values still report correctly. The PR also lacks before/after timings to demonstrate the optimization is in the critical path. Both leave the change TESTED-NOT-PROVED and the perf claim unmeasured.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the optimization strategy is sound — cheap prefilters bypassing expensive parsing — but execution is under-audited and the invariant 'prefilter accepts every value the walker would flag' is nowhere stated. The most serious finding is import-notation's 'url' branch, which inverts the guard logic and silently skips the validation case it was designed for. Secondary correctness concerns include asymmetric case flags in keyframe-selector-notation and mixed-value handling in font-weight-notation. Supporting issues: unescaped regex construction from keyword sets, an over-broad media-feature heuristic, and the absence of both targeted boundary tests and performance measurements. Accept with the listed fixes and added tests.
